To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
remittances have a positive impact on the poverty status of rural households in India.

(i) the incidence of poverty is lower in rural households receiving international remittances as compared to households not receiving any remittances, (ii) the incidence of extreme poverty is lower in households receiving international remittance as compared to households receiving internal remittances, which in turn are less poor than households receiving no remittance, and (iii) there is no difference in the incidence of poverty in rural households receiving internal remittance and households not receiving any transfer income.
remittances have a positive impact on poverty reduction in rural India.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the question of whether remittances help reduce the incidence of poverty and if so to what extent.
the impact of remittances in the context of rural India, and it provides a useful addition to the existing body of knowledge on migration and remittances.
the question of whether remittances are an important factor in the process of poverty alleviation and rural development in India.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the effect of remittance income is to reduce the incidence of poverty, but the effect is not very large.

the poverty alleviating effects of migration and remittances in India are not only real but also substantial, and that the benefits of migration and remittance income flow back to the origin communities.
while remittances are a significant source of income for rural households, their impact on poverty alleviation is not very significant.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
remittances from both internal and external sources are important in alleviating rural poverty.
while remittances do not seem to have any effect on rural household consumption levels, they do help to reduce the incidence of rural poverty.
remittances are a useful instrument for rural development in India.
The main takeaway from our work is that
remittance income can play a crucial role in reducing poverty among recipient rural Indian households.
the effect of remittance income in reducing poverty in rural India seems to be more pronounced among the poorer sections of the society.
the impact of remittances is contingent upon household characteristics, and hence, the poverty alleviating effect of remittanes may not be universal.
